en: The Apadāna of the Elder Paccāgamaniya Sakacintaniya Chapter, Number 3 I was a merchant in the city of Benares, Possessing great wealth and abundant riches. At that time, the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, Was dwelling in the city of Sāvatthī. Having heard of the Teacher’s arrival, I went forth with a great multitude of people. Having approached the Teacher, the Great Sage, I paid homage at his feet and sat to one side. Seated there, I listened to the Dhamma Spoken by the Teacher, the Knower of the World. Then, having heard the Dhamma from the Buddha, I developed a mind of faith toward him. With palms joined together in reverence, I spoke these words to the Blessed One: “O Blessed One, may you accept me As a lay follower who has taken refuge. The Teacher, the Great Sage, accepted me, And I departed from that very place. Having gone back to my own home, I gave away all my wealth in charity. I built a monastery for the Saṅgha, A dwelling place for the Community of Monks. Therein I provided robes, alms-food, Beds, seats, medicine, and other requisites. For twenty thousand years, I honored the Conqueror’s heirs. After passing away from that human state, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-Three. There I enjoyed divine pleasures, Surrounded by a host of celestial nymphs. From there, passing away after my lifespan ended, I was reborn among humans once again. In every birth I took, I was always born as a wealthy man. I possessed great power and authority, And I was never lacking in food or drink. Through the merit of that deed, I have attained this final existence. Now, as a monk, I dwell in peace, Having reached the goal of my practice. By the power of that wholesome deed, I have been freed from all suffering. This is the fruit of giving alms, And of building a dwelling for the Saṅgha. Thus did the Elder Paccāgamaniya Speak of his own past deeds. Having heard this account of his former life, One should strive to emulate his conduct. May all beings be well and happy! “At that time, on the bank of the river Sindhu,
I was a ruddy sheldrake;
my food consisted solely of pure water-moss.”
And well-restrained from evil deeds,
I saw the stainless Buddha going along the wind-swept path.
Taking a sal tree with my trunk,
I offered it to Vipassi;
whoever has faith in the Tathāgata—
Unshakable and well-established;
by that clarity of mind,
he does not go to a state of misery.
"Welcome indeed has come to me in the presence of the Best of Buddhas,
by means of this peaceful bird."
A good seed was sown by me.
In the ninety-first aeon,
that flower which I offered—
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
[She was] named Sucārudassanā.
These eight, all bearing the same name,
were mighty wheel-turning monarchs during the seventeenth aeon.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Paccāgamaniya spoke these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Paccāgamaniya.
